example.name: securing_spring_boot_api
example.scenario: Implementing TLS/mTLS and OAuth security for a new Spring Boot REST API that handles financial transactions.

requirements.requirement: OAuth 2.0 with PKCE for user authentication

step.implementation:
# application.yml server: port: 8443 ssl: enabled: true bundle: "server-cert" client-auth: need # Require client certificates for mTLS
spring: ssl: bundle: pem: server-cert: keystore: certificate: "classpath:certs/server-cert.pem" private-key: "classpath:certs/server-key.pem" truststore: certificate: "classpath:certs/ca-cert.pem"
security: oauth2: client: registration: banking-app: client-id: ${OAUTH_CLIENT_ID} client-secret: ${OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET} authorization-grant-type: authorization_code redirect-uri: "{baseUrl}/oauth2/callback/{registrationId}" scope: - openid - profile - transactions:write - accounts:read provider: banking-app: authorization-uri: https://auth.bank.example.com/oauth2/authorize token-uri: https://auth.bank.example.com/oauth2/token user-info-uri: https://auth.bank.example.com/oauth2/userinfo jwk-set-uri: https://auth.bank.example.com/oauth2/jwks

step.expected_outcome: No CRITICAL findings. WARNING for SSL bundle usage (expected, requires verification).

validation.check: Verify only approved algorithms (AES-256-GCM, RSA-3072, SHA-256)

step.action: Deploy to Kubernetes with TLS configuration
step.implementation:
# deployment.yaml apiVersion: apps/v1 kind: Deployment metadata: name: banking-api spec: replicas: 3 template: spec: containers: - name: banking-api image: banking-api:latest ports: - containerPort: 8443 name: https env: - name: OAUTH_CLIENT_ID valueFrom: secretKeyRef: name: oauth-credentials key: client-id - name: OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET valueFrom: secretKeyRef: name: oauth-credentials key: client-secret volumeMounts: - name: tls-certs mountPath: /app/certs readOnly: true volumes: - name: tls-certs secret: secretName: banking-api-tls
--- apiVersion: v1 kind: Service metadata: name: banking-api spec: type: ClusterIP ports: - port: 443 targetPort: 8443 protocol: TCP name: https selector: app: banking-api
--- apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1 kind: Ingress metadata: name: banking-api annotations: nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/ssl-protocols: "TLSv1.3 TLSv1.2" nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/ssl-ciphers: "ECDHE-RSA-AES256-GCM-SHA384:ECDHE-RSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256" nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/auth-tls-verify-client: "on" nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/auth-tls-secret: "default/client-ca" spec: tls: - hosts: - api.bank.example.com secretName: banking-api-ingress-tls rules: - host: api.bank.example.com http: paths: - path: / pathType: Prefix backend: service: name: banking-api port: number: 443

step.validation_script:
#!/bin/bash # validate-tls-config.sh
# Check certificate validity openssl x509 -in certs/server-cert.pem -noout -checkend 2592000 if [ $? -ne 0 ]; then echo "ERROR: Certificate expires within 30 days" exit 1 fi
# Verify certificate chain openssl verify -CAfile certs/ca-cert.pem certs/server-cert.pem if [ $? -ne 0 ]; then echo "ERROR: Certificate chain validation failed" exit 1 fi
# Check key permissions if [ "$(stat -c %a certs/server-key.pem)" != "600" ]; then echo "ERROR: Private key has insecure permissions" exit 1 fi
echo "Configuration validation passed"

step.test_script:
#!/bin/bash # test-mtls.sh
API_URL="https://api.bank.example.com/api/health"
# Test 1: No client certificate (should fail) echo "Test 1: No client certificate" curl -v $API_URL 2>&1 | grep "client certificate"
# Test 2: Valid client certificate (should succeed) echo "Test 2: Valid client certificate" curl --cert client.pem --key client-key.pem $API_URL
# Test 3: Invalid client certificate (should fail) echo "Test 3: Invalid client certificate" curl --cert invalid-client.pem --key invalid-key.pem $API_URL 2>&1 | grep "certificate"
# Test 4: Revoked client certificate (should fail) echo "Test 4: Revoked client certificate" curl --cert revoked-client.pem --key revoked-key.pem $API_URL 2>&1 | grep "revoked"

step.monitoring_configuration:
# prometheus-rules.yml groups: - name: tls_monitoring interval: 4h rules: - alert: TLSConfigurationChanged expr: tls_config_hash != tls_config_baseline_hash annotations: summary: "TLS configuration drift detected"
- alert: CertificateExpiringSoon expr: (cert_expiry_timestamp - time()) < 2592000 annotations: summary: "Certificate expires in less than 30 days"
- alert: WeakCipherDetected expr: weak_cipher_offered == 1 annotations: summary: "Weak cipher suite detected on endpoint"

example.name: securing_nginx_reverse_proxy
example.scenario: Configuring nginx as a reverse proxy with hardened TLS for banking applications.

step.action: Create nginx configuration with TLS hardening

step.implementation:
# deploy-nginx.yml --- - name: Deploy nginx with TLS configuration hosts: web_servers become: yes
vars: nginx_cert_path: /etc/nginx/certs cert_expiry_days: 30
tasks: - name: Install nginx apt: name: nginx state: present update_cache: yes
- name: Create certificate directory file: path: "{{ nginx_cert_path }}" state: directory mode: '0755'
- name: Copy TLS certificates copy: src: "{{ item.src }}" dest: "{{ nginx_cert_path }}/{{ item.dest }}" mode: "{{ item.mode }}" loop: - { src: 'certs/server-cert.pem', dest: 'server-cert.pem', mode: '0644' } - { src: 'certs/server-key.pem', dest: 'server-key.pem', mode: '0600' } - { src: 'certs/client-ca.pem', dest: 'client-ca.pem', mode: '0644' } - { src: 'certs/ca-chain.pem', dest: 'ca-chain.pem', mode: '0644' } - { src: 'certs/crl.pem', dest: 'crl.pem', mode: '0644' } notify: reload nginx
- name: Validate certificate expiration command: openssl x509 -in {{ nginx_cert_path }}/server-cert.pem -noout -checkend {{ cert_expiry_days * 86400 }} register: cert_check failed_when: cert_check.rc != 0 changed_when: false
- name: Validate certificate chain command: openssl verify -CAfile {{ nginx_cert_path }}/ca-chain.pem {{ nginx_cert_path }}/server-cert.pem register: chain_check failed_when: chain_check.rc != 0 changed_when: false
- name: Deploy nginx configuration template: src: nginx.conf.j2 dest: /etc/nginx/nginx.conf validate: 'nginx -t -c %s' notify: reload nginx
- name: Ensure nginx is running service: name: nginx state: started enabled: yes
handlers: - name: reload nginx service: name: nginx state: reloaded

step.validation_script:
#!/bin/bash # validate-nginx-tls.sh
HOST="api.bank.example.com" PORT=443
echo "=== TLS Protocol Validation ===" openssl s_client -connect $HOST:$PORT -tls1_3 < /dev/null 2>&1 | grep "Protocol" openssl s_client -connect $HOST:$PORT -tls1_2 < /dev/null 2>&1 | grep "Protocol"
echo "=== Cipher Suite Validation ===" openssl s_client -connect $HOST:$PORT -cipher 'ECDHE-RSA-AES256-GCM-SHA384' < /dev/null 2>&1 | grep "Cipher"
echo "=== Certificate Validation ===" openssl s_client -connect $HOST:$PORT -showcerts < /dev/null 2>&1 | openssl x509 -noout -subject -issuer -dates
echo "=== HSTS Header Validation ===" curl -I https://$HOST 2>&1 | grep -i "strict-transport-security"
echo "=== mTLS Validation ===" curl -v https://$HOST 2>&1 | grep "client certificate"

test.name: pkce_required
test.test_script:
# Test without PKCE (should fail) curl -X POST "https://auth.bank.example.com/oauth2/authorize" \ -d "client_id=banking-app" \ -d "redirect_uri=https://app.bank.example.com/oauth2/callback" \ -d "response_type=code" \ -d "scope=openid profile" \ -d "state=random_state"
# Expected: Error indicating PKCE is required

test.name: redirect_uri_validation
test.test_script:
# Test with invalid redirect_uri (should fail) curl -X POST "https://auth.bank.example.com/oauth2/authorize" \ -d "client_id=banking-app" \ -d "redirect_uri=https://evil.com/callback" \ -d "response_type=code" \ -d "scope=openid profile" \ -d "state=random_state" \ -d "code_challenge=challenge" \ -d "code_challenge_method=S256"
# Expected: Error indicating invalid redirect_uri

test.name: token_expiration
test.test_script:
# Get access token TOKEN=$(curl -X POST "https://auth.bank.example.com/oauth2/token" \ -d "grant_type=authorization_code" \ -d "code=$AUTH_CODE" \ -d "redirect_uri=https://app.bank.example.com/oauth2/callback" \ -d "client_id=banking-app" \ -d "client_secret=secret" \ -d "code_verifier=$CODE_VERIFIER" \ | jq -r '.access_token')
# Wait 16 minutes (token expires after 15 minutes) sleep 960
# Try to use expired token (should fail) curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \ "https://api.bank.example.com/api/accounts"
# Expected: 401 Unauthorized

test.name: refresh_token_rotation
test.test_script:
# Use refresh token RESPONSE=$(curl -X POST "https://auth.bank.example.com/oauth2/token" \ -d "grant_type=refresh_token" \ -d "refresh_token=$REFRESH_TOKEN" \ -d "client_id=banking-app" \ -d "client_secret=secret")
NEW_REFRESH_TOKEN=$(echo $RESPONSE | jq -r '.refresh_token')
# Try to use old refresh token again (should fail) curl -X POST "https://auth.bank.example.com/oauth2/token" \ -d "grant_type=refresh_token" \ -d "refresh_token=$REFRESH_TOKEN" \ -d "client_id=banking-app" \ -d "client_secret=secret"
# Expected: Error indicating token was already used

example.name: certificate_lifecycle_management
example.scenario: Implementing automated certificate lifecycle management with monitoring and renewal for banking infrastructure.

step.implementation:
# certificate-inventory.yml certificates: - name: api-server-cert type: server path: /etc/certs/api-server-cert.pem key_path: /etc/certs/api-server-key.pem domains: - api.bank.example.com expiry_alert_days: [60, 30, 14, 7] renewal_method: acme
- name: mtls-client-cert type: client path: /etc/certs/mtls-client-cert.pem key_path: /etc/certs/mtls-client-key.pem ca: internal-ca expiry_alert_days: [60, 30, 14, 7] renewal_method: internal
- name: code-signing-cert type: signing path: /etc/certs/code-signing-cert.pem key_path: /etc/certs/code-signing-key.pem expiry_alert_days: [90, 60, 30] renewal_method: manual

#!/usr/bin/env python3 # monitor-certificates.py
import subprocess import datetime import json import yaml from pathlib import Path
def check_certificate_expiry(cert_path): """Check certificate expiration date""" cmd = ['openssl', 'x509', '-in', cert_path, '-noout', '-enddate'] result = subprocess.run(cmd, capture_output=True, text=True)
if result.returncode != 0: return None
# Parse expiry date expiry_str = result.stdout.strip().replace('notAfter=', '') expiry_date = datetime.datetime.strptime(expiry_str, '%b %d %H:%M:%S %Y %Z')
days_until_expiry = (expiry_date - datetime.datetime.now()).days return days_until_expiry
def check_certificate_chain(cert_path, ca_path): """Verify certificate chain""" cmd = ['openssl', 'verify', '-CAfile', ca_path, cert_path] result = subprocess.run(cmd, capture_output=True, text=True) return result.returncode == 0
def main(): # Load certificate inventory with open('certificate-inventory.yml') as f: inventory = yaml.safe_load(f)
alerts = []
for cert in inventory['certificates']: cert_path = cert['path']
# Check expiration days_until_expiry = check_certificate_expiry(cert_path)
if days_until_expiry is None: alerts.append({ 'severity': 'CRITICAL', 'certificate': cert['name'], 'message': 'Certificate file not found or invalid' }) continue
# Check against alert thresholds for threshold in cert['expiry_alert_days']: if days_until_expiry <= threshold: severity = 'CRITICAL' if days_until_expiry <= 7 else 'WARNING' alerts.append({ 'severity': severity, 'certificate': cert['name'], 'message': f'Certificate expires in {days_until_expiry} days', 'expiry_days': days_until_expiry, 'renewal_method': cert['renewal_method'] }) break
# Output alerts if alerts: print(json.dumps(alerts, indent=2)) return 1 else: print("All certificates valid") return 0
if __name__ == '__main__': exit(main())

step.action: Implement automated renewal with Let's Encrypt
step.implementation:
#!/bin/bash # renew-certificates.sh
CERT_DIR="/etc/certs" ACME_DIR="/var/lib/acme" DOMAINS="api.bank.example.com"
# Request new certificate using certbot certbot certonly \ --webroot \ --webroot-path=/var/www/html \ --email security@bank.example.com \ --agree-tos \ --no-eff-email \ --domains $DOMAINS \ --cert-name api-server-cert
# Copy certificates to application directory cp /etc/letsencrypt/live/api-server-cert/fullchain.pem $CERT_DIR/api-server-cert.pem cp /etc/letsencrypt/live/api-server-cert/privkey.pem $CERT_DIR/api-server-key.pem
# Set proper permissions chmod 644 $CERT_DIR/api-server-cert.pem chmod 600 $CERT_DIR/api-server-key.pem
# Reload services systemctl reload nginx kubectl rollout restart deployment/banking-api
# Verify new certificate ./validate-certificate.sh $CERT_DIR/api-server-cert.pem

# prometheus-certificate-exporter.yml apiVersion: v1 kind: ConfigMap metadata: name: certificate-exporter-config data: config.yml: | certificates: - name: api_server_cert path: /certs/api-server-cert.pem - name: mtls_client_cert path: /certs/mtls-client-cert.pem
--- apiVersion: apps/v1 kind: Deployment metadata: name: certificate-exporter spec: replicas: 1 template: spec: containers: - name: certificate-exporter image: enix/x509-certificate-exporter:latest volumeMounts: - name: certs mountPath: /certs readOnly: true - name: config mountPath: /config volumes: - name: certs secret: secretName: tls-certificates - name: config configMap: name: certificate-exporter-config
--- # Prometheus alert rules apiVersion: v1 kind: ConfigMap metadata: name: prometheus-certificate-alerts data: certificate-alerts.yml: | groups: - name: certificates rules: - alert: CertificateExpiringSoon expr: x509_cert_not_after - time() < 2592000 labels: severity: warning annotations: summary: "Certificate {{ $labels.subject_CN }} expires in less than 30 days"
- alert: CertificateExpiringCritical expr: x509_cert_not_after - time() < 604800 labels: severity: critical annotations: summary: "Certificate {{ $labels.subject_CN }} expires in less than 7 days"
- alert: CertificateExpired expr: x509_cert_not_after - time() < 0 labels: severity: critical annotations: summary: "Certificate {{ $labels.subject_CN }} has expired"

# Kubernetes CronJob for automated renewal apiVersion: batch/v1 kind: CronJob metadata: name: certificate-renewal spec: schedule: "0 2 * * *" # Daily at 2 AM jobTemplate: spec: template: spec: containers: - name: cert-renewal image: certbot/certbot:latest command: - /bin/sh - -c - | # Check certificates and renew if needed python3 /scripts/monitor-certificates.py
# Renew certificates expiring within 30 days certbot renew --deploy-hook "/scripts/deploy-renewed-cert.sh" volumeMounts: - name: scripts mountPath: /scripts - name: letsencrypt mountPath: /etc/letsencrypt volumes: - name: scripts configMap: name: cert-renewal-scripts - name: letsencrypt persistentVolumeClaim: claimName: letsencrypt-data restartPolicy: OnFailure
